newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian defence chief tells wife: 'no pay today'.
newsitem.headline: Russian defence chief tells wife: 'no pay today'.

text.p: Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov says he will refuse to draw his salary until the country's armed forces are paid their long overdue arrears.
The army newspaper Red Star said on Thursday unpaid wages and "catastrophic" living conditions were driving Russian servicemen to suicide.
Red Star said one non-commissioned officer from the far northwest Kaliningard region committed suicide leaving a note, saying simply: "I am tired".
Another serviceman from the same region hanged himself. "The reasons were identical: long overdue salaries," Red Star said.
Rodionov, the man in charge of paying the army, told readers of another newspaper, Komsomolskaya Pravda, he would suffer alongside his men.
"I begin and end my working day with this problem," Rodionov, who was appointed in July, was quoted as saying.
"I go home and my wife asks me: 'Did you bring your pay, Pa? And I can't tell her anything. And I tell her: 'When the army gets paid, then I'll get paid'."

Red Star said the military command of the Baltic fleet wrote last week to Rodionov's patron in the Kremlin, Alexander Lebed, secretary of the Security Council, telling him about long outstanding arrears in wage payments in the Kaliningrad region.
"Officers often ask the military command to let them work once a week 'on the side' to earn bread for their families," the newspaper said.

Red Star gave no figures, but Interfax news agency said in July that some 423 Russian soldiers had committed suicide last year. It gave the main cause as the "dyedovshchina" - a widespread and notorious system of brutality and bullying of younger recruits by older soldiers.
